problem:
From **left to right,** the $x$-intercepts of the hyperbola $\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{18}-\frac{(y-3)^{2}}{9}=1$ are

$($
{{field-1}}, 
{{field-2}} $)\,$
and 
$\,($
{{field-3}}, 
{{field-4}} $).$

feedback.worked_solution:
To find the $x$-intercepts of the hyperbola, we substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the hyperbola and solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(y-3)^{2}}{9}-\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{16} & =1 \\ \frac{(0-3)^{2}}{9}-\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{16} & =1 \\ 1-\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{16} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-1)^{2}}{16} & =0 \\ (x-1)^{2} & =0 \\ x-1 & =0 \\ x & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $x$-intercept is $(1,0).$
